children.text: *[caption on top of video]: When the video appears on the person’s screen, it is immediately presented with text across the top of the video saying, “installing a wig (or trying my hardest to),”establishing the purpose/tone of the video. Rather than posting the video with no context, and leaving the audience to interpret the video as a serious wig tutorial, Vanillamace uses the phrase “or trying my hardest to” to sort of make fun of her own lack of expertise and prepare the audience for an imperfect process. This makes the purpose of the video less about teaching her viewers how to install a wig, and more about entertaining them through her experience as if she was taking everyone along the journey with her. Using pathos, Vanilla incorporates her humour and personality in her content and the way it is presented, which gives viewers a reason to continue watching even if they are not interested in learning about installing a wig.

The visual modality of the video creates a more casual/personal aesthetic through Vanillamace’s restroom background. Instead of making a professional studio backdrop or filming in a studio, she installs her wig in an everyday space where one would normally get ready. This unpolished aesthetic makes the video feel like viewers are hanging out with her, rather than watching an influencer video with production behind it. The combination of the livestream and her direct interaction with the chat helps to reinforce her “internet bestie” persona across platforms. The familiar aesthetic also appeals through pathos, creating feelings of comfort, which strengthens her perceived authenticity and reliability with her viewers.

When Vanillamace puts on her durag, she prefaces that it is “only done in my own home,” which shows that she is aware of how wearing it could be interpreted as cultural appropriation. Someone in the livestream chat even comments “CANCELLED,” to emphasize her joke. This demonstrates a constraint of having a large online platform, where actions could be easily taken out of context or interpreted differently by people outside of her intended audience. Because TikTok can circulate her content beyond her regular followers, she prepares for possible criticism and addresses it before the viewers do. Her humour helps guide her awareness of the cultural sensitivity, while maintaining her unfiltered personality that is associated with her brand.

Around the same time frame here, there is a layering of the audience and cancel culture as mentioned previously. Vanillamace’s intended audience seems to be people who are already familiar with her humour, personality, and the community she has built in her live streams. When she jokes about wearing the durag in her own home and someone in the Twitch says “CANCELLED”, it also makes it known that her regular viewers understand the context and participate in the joke, rather than taking the situation literally. However, once this clip is posted onto TikTok, her actual audience is now more broad, and can include people who have never seen her content before. Her intended vs actual audiences can allow for the same joke to be misinterpreted, depending on the viewer’s familiarity with Vanillamace’s personality and her online persona.

TikTok provides Vanillamace with the affordance of recycling her content for her long Twitch streams, into shorter and more engaging clips for her TikTok audience. Rather than uploading the livestream exactly as it happened, she can edit clips from the Twitch stream together, and incorporate her own cuts, zoom ins, and tag overlaps, which emphasizes her exaggerated facial expressions and funny pauses/reactions. The overlapping edits are also a genre strategy on TikTok where fast paced and layered editing helps to grab and maintain the viewers’ attention.  TikTok also lets her upload content edited outside of the platform, which gives her more freedom over how she wants to present her content. These affordances allow her to expand her audience beyond just Twitch, and still maintain her humour and unfiltered personality that is built around her brand.

Vanillamace uses ethos in this section by allowing the audience to see moments where she is unsure of what she is doing instead of acting as if she is an expert. Her credibility with her audience becomes less from having professional knowledge, and more from installing and styling a wig more from her perceived authentic self. Making mistakes, being uncertain about how to cut the hair, and the reactions in the video help support her unfiltered persona that she has built across multiple platforms. This can make viewers feel as if they’re seeing a more genuine version of her, rather than watching a performative influencer act as if they knew exactly what they were doing.

Here, Vanillamace’s facial expressions and body language function as visual messages of the video, which can communicate more than what she is actually physically saying. When something does not go as expected during her wig installation, she pauses or gives an exaggerated facial expression before she continues her process. Then, when viewers see her reactions, it does not require her to vocalize that she is confused or surprised over what is happening, but her physical delivery helps communicate that she is. This also appeals through pathos as the audience is experiencing her reactions with her, rather than hearing her describe how she is feeling after. Her expressions become a rhetorical device on their own, helping her communicate her emotions of each moment without relying on words coming out of her mouth.

*[entire video]: Although the perceived purpose of the video seems to be in the realm of a “get ready with me” style video, Vanillamace does not follow the traditional conventions of a step by step beauty tutorial. She does not list a bunch of products she is using, clearly explaining each step, or presenting herself as someone who is teaching the audience the correct way of installing a wig. However, the wig installation serves as an activity for the viewers to follow while her commentary and reactions is the main focus. This shifts the purpose of the video from beauty content, to more entertaining and personality centered content. The wig invites more interaction with the audience rather than being the only reason to watch. This goes to show how an influencer can use a genre while changing its purpose to still fit their personal brand.
